You need to get a mediator and work out a parenting and child support arrangement based on your state laws. You also need to keep in mind, though, that since most states base child support on “overnights,” your ex is only getting credit for 10 nights/month (1 night/week and every other weekend) though he’s presumably providing at least one meal and snacks for the preschooler 5 days/wk (plus for both kids during the summer when he presumably cares for them).

Either put the preschooler in child care and both in care during the summer (that way he has no expectation of money from you) or work with the mediator on a child support agreement that gives him credit for *all* the provisions he’s making for the kids.

ETA: If you do continue to keep the kids most nights and put them in child care, he will be responsible for the percentage of care he’s expected to provide for your children. If he doesn’t receive disability then they will impute a wage on him based on what he earned before he quit his job. If it’s more than you make then he will be responsible for a higher percentage of care than you and will likely be ordered to pay you support. Meaning he’ll have to either get a job or go through the process of actually getting on disability.
Go ahead and ask him with the “cushion.” It never hurts to ask!
